title: Expected Opportunity vs Actual Production: do trailing PPR residuals predict next-game / next-3-game output beyond workload and production?
hypothesis: H1 (persistence): trailing residual (actual PPR - ffopportunity expected PPR) carries information about future output beyond trailing workload and production. H2 (regression): after controls, a negative trailing residual predicts a better-than-baseline future (bounce-back) and a positive one a worse-than-baseline future. Null: residual adds nothing.
sources: ffverse/ffopportunity ep_weekly 2020-2025 (public release v1.0.0-data; total_fantasy_points_exp / total_fantasy_points are PPR)
population: QB/RB/WR/TE regular-season player-games. Prediction origin = a completed game t; requires >=k prior appearances (window k) and the targeted future appearances. Logs run across seasons per player; the split is by the season of the origin game.

splits.note: dev fit -> validation 2024. Then refit on 2021-2024 and score 2025 exactly once with the frozen specification. 2026 YTD is descriptive only (5 weeks).

features.res_k: mean over last k appearances (k in {3,6}) of actual PPR - expected PPR (ffopportunity)
features.exp_k: mean expected PPR over the same k games (workload proxy)
features.act_k: mean actual PPR over the same k games (production)
features.vol_k: mean targets, carries and pass attempts over the same k games (raw workload)
features.act_12: mean actual PPR over the last 12 appearances (longer production baseline)

horizons: mean of next 3 appearances (all 3 required, same season as origin or later; no gaps filter)

models.baseline: OLS per position: y ~ act_k + vol_k(3 terms) + act_12
models.challenger: baseline + exp_k (identical to adding res_k since res_k = act_k - exp_k; coefficient on res_k reported as b_res = b_act - b_exp decomposition: challenger fitted as y ~ res_k + exp_k + vol_k + act_12)
models.note: Fixed specification, no tuning, no regularisation. Hyperparameters nothing; windows k=3 and k=6 are both reported, not selected.

family: 4 outcomes x 2 horizons x 2 windows = 16 tests per position; Bonferroni 95% intervals (alpha 0.05/16) for any claim of 'predictive'.
inference: player-clustered bootstrap (2000 resamples) on (a) per-row squared-error difference baseline minus challenger out of sample and (b) the b_res coefficient fitted on the training window.

decision_rule.PREDICTIVE: Out-of-sample MSE reduction >= 1% in BOTH 2024 validation and 2025 holdout, and the Bonferroni cluster-bootstrap CI of the 2025 holdout squared-error difference excludes 0 (favouring challenger), and the sign of b_res matches in dev and in the 2021-24 refit.
decision_rule.DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY: Everything else: residual is reported as a description of the past, not a forecast.
decision_rule.NO_EFFECT_CLAIM: Only if the CI excludes a 1% improvement; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.

exploratory_not_countable: Split of the residual into touchdown part (6*TD diff, 4 for passing TD folded in via total_touchdown_diff*6) and non-touchdown part; same models. Labelled exploratory and cannot support a PREDICTIVE label.
leakage: All features use games up to and including the origin game; targets are strictly later games; ffopportunity expected values are model outputs fitted on earlier seasons and not retrained in-season (ffopportunity v1.0.0 was fitted on pre-2021 data per its documentation: stated as an assumption, not verified).
caveats: Not a betting-return test. No market prices are used.
Pre-registration is a committed document date, not a cryptographic timestamp; spec hash is printed by the study script.
